floorReductionsTouched: Reduction 1 — the nine non-catalogue C9-CAP keys (formerly EC-2): carried verbatim in F46 (the c9Floor branch) and F91 row 1 (the compensating fences, split by exemption and by mint path). No key added, none removed, no value changed.

The subjectFloor retention for non-HANDOFF exempt intents is preserved exactly, so control.run.cancel keeps BOUND_CLIENT.
No third reduction is introduced. F51's C9_FLOOR_BASELINE build assertion and F49's vetoes are the mechanisms that make a third one fail the build.

EC-4's FLOOR_EXEMPT set — touched at §2.6.15 SOURCE.3 only. The nine are enumerated by name; SOURCE_READ contributes ANONYMOUS (not SESSION_VERIFIED); the residual-fence split by HANDOFF/FLOOR_EXEMPT and by run-bearing/run-less mint path is reproduced word for word.

EC-4's five FLOOR_EXEMPT intents — carried verbatim into R3.4.7 (the predicate, the three build vetoes, the five-row census table) and R3.4.8's second table row. subjectFloor is retained for every non-HANDOFF exempt intent; SENSITIVE_DEST excludes every consent/identity handoff; no third reduction is introduced.

EC-2's nine C9-CAP keys / c9Floor — NOT touched by this section. §4.5.4 step 1 reads verification_floor as a value; no rule here computes or narrows c9Floor, and no throwing accessor is introduced (c9Registry.tryGet with a fail-closed default is the only registry read).

Re-stating the five tables inside §1.8 would have created a second canonical site for a security-critical function and risked a third floor reduction.
